[ASSISTANT_SAID] Packing lunch is a great start to saving money and is a fantastic habit to develop.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended budgeting apps and tools include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Mint: A free personal finance app that tracks spending, creates budgets, and sets financial goals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Personal Capital: A free financial management app for tracking income, expenses, investments, and debts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. YNAB (You Need a Budget): A paid app (free trial available) that helps manage finances by assigning jobs to every dollar.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Spreadsheets (Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel): A free and customizable option for creating a budget template.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Pocketbook: A free budgeting app for tracking income and expenses, setting budget goals, and receiving bill reminders.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Wally: A free app for tracking expenses, income, and savings goals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Spendee: A free app for tracking expenses by categorizing transactions and offering budgeting features.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Quicken: A paid personal finance software for tracking spending, creating budgets, and managing investments.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Budgeting apps from banks: Many banks offer their own budgeting apps.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested factors to consider when choosing an app: ease of use, features, compatibility, cost, and integration.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Emphasized the importance of consistency and regularly tracking expenses for successful budgeting.
